﴿Say: He is Allah, the One.﴾ The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about his Lord, and so ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ was revealed. In the grammatical analysis, ﴿اللَّه﴾ (Allah) is the khabar (predicate) of ﴿هُوَ﴾ (He), and ﴿أحَد﴾ (ahad, "One") is either a badal (substitute, in apposition) for it, or a second khabar (predicate).
﴿Allah, the Eternal Refuge﴾: a mubtada' (subject of the nominal sentence) and khabar (predicate). That is, the One who is sought in needs, constantly.
{"Lam yalid" (He begets not) — because of the negation of His being of the same kind (as offspring). "Wa lam yulad" (nor is He begotten) — because of the negation of origination (hudūth) from Him.

﴿And there is none comparable to Him.﴾ That is, equivalent and similar. "Lahu" (for Him) is related to "kufuwan" (comparable), its grammatical complement (muta'allaq), and it was placed before "kufuwan" because it is the focus of the negation. "Ahad" (anyone), which is the subject (ism) of "yakun" (is), was delayed from its predicate (khabar) for the sake of the fasilah (the verse-ending rhyme).
